answer: Drop the single highest and single lowest score on every grading panel and settle the verdict on the average of what's left. On a five-seat jury that's the middle three. Say a farm account gets seated on a sibling's thin answer about sable pelts in an oasis market and hands it a 3 while the others give 1s. That 3 is the first thing cut, so it sends no signal at all. To move a verdict the farm needs two of its accounts on the same panel, and since seats come from the whole pool, landing pairs takes far more aged accounts than landing one. Honest graders don't change a thing.
